## Description

Newton interpolation represents the interpolating polynomial in divided-difference form,

$$
P_n(x)=a_0 + a_1(x-x_0)+a_2(x-x_0)(x-x_1)+\cdots+a_n\prod_{j=0}^{n-1}(x-x_j),
$$

where $a_k=f[x_0,\ldots,x_k]$ are divided differences. For the same nodes and data, Newton and Lagrange forms produce the same polynomial; they differ only in representation and numerical workflow.

Cases 01–29 below intentionally reuse the same interpolation cases as the [Lagrange page](../lagrange-polynomial-interpolation-and-approximation/index.qmd), matching the legacy Mathews case ordering; the Lagrange page gives each case's function and node interval.

## Animations

Cases 01–29 each show the interpolant on 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14 and 16 equally spaced nodes (degree 1 to 5, then 7, 9, 11, 13 and 15) for a fixed function and node interval, with nodes at both ends of the interval.

The shared script draws this same polynomial but evaluates it in the first barycentric (Lagrange) form, not by divided differences. The last case on this page has its own script, which builds the Newton form from divided differences.

### Divided differences: $f(x)=\cos x$, nodes $x_k = k\pi/3$ on $[0, 2\pi]$

**Behavior:** Each frame adds the next node and one more Newton term $a_n\prod_{j<n}(x-x_j)$; the coefficients already found do not change. The divided differences are $a_0,\ldots,a_6 = 1,\ -\tfrac{3}{2\pi},\ -\tfrac{9}{4\pi^2},\ \tfrac{9}{2\pi^3},\ -\tfrac{27}{16\pi^4},\ -\tfrac{81}{80\pi^5},\ \tfrac{81}{80\pi^6}$. For degrees 1 to 4 the polynomial leaves the plot to the right of the newest node; with all seven nodes (degree 6) the largest error on $[0, 2\pi]$ is 0.0071.

[Julia source](newtpolyaa.jl)

![Newton interpolation of cos x on [0, 2π], adding one node x_k = kπ/3 per frame from degree 0 (1 node) to degree 6 (7 nodes); the dashed polynomial passes through every node and matches cos x within 0.0071 at degree 6.](newtpolyaa.gif)
